1. Verify internal consistency: sum the line items ($18.38 + $23.29 + $118.95) to confirm they equal $160.62, and check that the meter-read difference (22,882 − 21,997 = 885 kWh) matches billed energy use; any mismatch flags a possible billing error.  
2. Compute the total dollar change: current total ($160.62) − last month total ($226.04) = −$65.42.  
3. Separate fixed and variable charges: treat the $18.38 customer charge as fixed; derive current variable rate from ($23.29 + $118.95) / 885 kWh, and infer last month’s variable rate from ($226.04 − $18.38) / 1,292 kWh.  
4. Calculate price_usd from any difference between the two periods’ variable rates applied to usage; calculate days_usd from the one-day billing-period difference (31 vs 30) only if the fixed charge is prorated per day, otherwise set to 0.  
5. Set weather_usd to 0 because no temperature or weather data is provided to isolate a weather effect.  
6. Derive usage_usd as the remaining change after price, days, and weather (equivalently, value the −407 kWh usage difference at the applicable rate).  
7. Conclude on billing_error_suspected: true with an estimated dollar amount if step 1 reveals inconsistencies; otherwise false with billing_error_usd = null.
